_comments: ActivitySyncRunDetail can hold encrypted fragments of messages deliberately NOT ingested.
CodeGen emits UI read + Integration CRUD for every new entity; nobody chose that here.
Amith's ruling is about read: no role other than Developer may read this entity.
Developer keeps the CodeGen CRUD row. UI is all zeros.
Integration keeps CanCreate so a scheduled ingest can append audit rows; CanRead/Update/Delete stay 0.
The engine does not pick a role — ActivitySyncEngine.Run takes contextUser from the caller.
Roles with no EntityPermission row are already denied; UI and Integration are the ones CodeGen granted.
Field-level security on CapturedContent: MJ is implementing EntityFieldPermission. Assume it.
Until that table exists, the entity-level deny is the control. Do not split the table.
